legend: The Tommyknockers (Cornish miners' folklore, Colorado gold mines, USA)
lines: Deep in a Colorado gold mine, a miner stops swinging his pick.
He hears it again: tap, tap, tap, from inside the rock.
Cornish miners carried the legend across the ocean in the eighteen hundreds.
They called them knockers, little spirits who live below the ground.
Some say their knocking warns of a cave-in before it happens.
Others say they love tricks, hiding tools and blowing out candles.
So miners always left a crust of their pasty behind for the knockers.
One man who laughed at them found his candle blown out in the dark.
Next time you hear tapping in a wall, will you leave a crumb?
title: The Tiny Spirits Who Knock Inside Gold Mines #shorts
description:
Cornish miners brought the Tommyknockers to the American West: tiny spirits whose tapping in the rock was said to warn of a cave-in.
